description.summary: share this computer's mouse and keyboard with another

protocol.description:
Lets a program take this computer's mouse and keyboard while the pointer is over on another computer, as Flow does. Offered on the Wayland socket of a plugin allowed "capture", and to programs outside every box.
The program names the side of the screens the other computer is on. When the pointer is pushed against that side, past the edge, the compositor hides the pointer, takes the pointer and keyboard from every window, sends "activated", and then hands every movement, button, scroll and key to the program until it sends "release", or until the compositor ends it itself ("deactivated"): the screen locked, or the person held Ctrl, Alt and Shift together for one second.
Version 2 adds two requests: "take", to cross at once without a push (so the program can cross when the person asks it to, by a key), and "set_mode", to turn pushing off so that crossing only ever happens by "take". A compositor that offers only version 1 has neither.

description.summary: no more captures will be asked for

request.name: get_capture

description.summary: cross to another computer at this side

request.description: Asks for the pointer to cross at the given side. A program may hold several captures at once, at most one for each side (up to four, for up to four computers). A newer capture for a side takes the place of an older one for that side only ("unavailable", taken, to the older); arming one side never disarms another. Only one side is capturing at a time: its events, and the program's release, come on the capture of the side that crossed.

description.summary: one side the pointer may cross at
stop; the mouse and keyboard come back if taken

request.name: release

description.summary: give the mouse and keyboard back

request.description: The pointer comes back just inside the side it left by, at "along", from 0 (the top or left end of that side) to 1 (the bottom or right end). Ignored when not active.

entry.name: not_now
entry.summary: a take was asked for when it cannot be: the screen is locked, a button is held, a question is showing, the mouse and keyboard are already taken, or too many takes were asked for in a second

entry.name: not_asked
entry.summary: the person did not just ask for this: a program in a box may take only within five seconds of its own shortcut, ring item or ring icon being used, once

entry.name: push
entry.summary: a push against the armed side crosses (the default)

entry.name: manual
entry.summary: a push never crosses; only take does

request.name: take

description.summary: cross now, as a push would

request.description: Starts capturing at once, as a push against that side would have, wherever the pointer is: the pointer is hidden where it is, the windows are told the pointer and keyboard have gone, and everything goes to the program until it releases. "side" is the side the other computer is on, as in get_capture (1 left, 2 right, 3 top, 4 bottom); "activated" follows, and a later release brings the pointer back just inside that side, level with where it was. Refused with "unavailable" when another capture has taken the place of this one (taken), and when it cannot be done now (not_now), and for a program in a box that the person has not just run by its own shortcut, ring item or ring icon (not_asked). Not held back by the corner guard, which is for pushes.

request.name: set_mode

description.summary: whether pushing crosses, or only take does

request.description: Applies to every capture of the program. A program starts in push mode, and stays in the mode it set for as long as it holds a capture.

description.summary: the pointer will not cross at this side
the side is armed; a push there crosses

event.name: activated

description.summary: the mouse and keyboard are now the program's

event.description: "along" says where along the side the pointer left, from 0 to 1, as in release.

description.summary: the pointer moved by this much, in the desktop's units
a button, by the kernel's number; state 1 pressed, 0 let go

event.name: axis

description.summary: scrolling: axis 0 up and down, 1 across

event.description: "value" is in the desktop's units, "v120" a wheel's clicks in 120ths, or 0 when it gave none.

description.summary: a key, by the kernel's number; state 1 pressed, 0 let go

entry.name: safety_keys
entry.summary: Ctrl, Alt and Shift were held for a second

entry.name: question
entry.summary: a question from Trindle itself came up, which only the person may answer

description.summary: the mouse and keyboard are this computer's again
